question.text: 'Nalanda India AIF' is being structured as a trust. The tax counsel insists the trust must be of a specific sub-type for clear tax treatment. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate trust sub-type for an AIF in India?

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.4 Alternative 1: the preferred AIF trust type is 'irrevocably settled, determinate' private trust. Determinacy means each beneficiary's share is ascertainable (achieved via unit capital). Irrevocability vests ownership permanently with the trust. The Trap: Options A and D mix 'public' (charitable) with investment pooling — inapt. Options B and A introduce revocability and indeterminacy — both violate the tax determinacy requirement. Cross-Exam Context: XVI (Taxation) tests the Section 161/164 trust taxation logic behind determinacy. XIX-C tests the structural consequence (unitisation). Manager's Pro-Tip: Document beneficial interest clearly in the trust deed using unit classes — ambiguity here can cause the Assessing Officer to treat the trust as indeterminate and deny pass-through.
